final: So there was this guy in college I had a crush on. I knew he liked me. He always sat next to me in class, and like, the way he looked at me. But he never said he liked me. Not once. So annoying, right?

I used to think that Grand Theft Auto was sexist, but now that we finally got GTA 6 and there's a female co-lead! And the fact that it's teaching guys to be better boyfriends, like, this is amazing. I'm definitely going to go get a PS5 real quick and start playing. Can't wait!

I know I should only give movies 5 stars on Letterboxd if they're critically acclaimed or if they've affected me in some way. But the fact that I'm rating super awful camp movies 5 stars is hilarious, isn't it?
I know I'm supposed to let the AI models write the prompts for you to answer, but like, they're never going to get my voice the way I talk, you know? Like, aren't you glad that I did this?
I know I'm supposed to go to the gym right now, but I'm getting so much done. Like, no, I'll go later or tomorrow. This is too much fun.

I know I should just post these pictures from the Warriors game. I have a photo of Steph Curry literally looking at my phone. And yet I don't want to post right now. I don't like curating my life for other people to watch. But yeah, I'm supposed to share with people. Except the algorithm doesn't even show my posts to my followers anymore.
Riding the cable car up Hyde Street at night is the one time I feel like I actually live here and I'm not just paying rent. But I know, cable cars are only for tourists.

I really love abstract art. It's just colors, and colors are numbers, and the spatial positions of the colors in respect to each other. Does it mean anything when I look at it? No, I mean, I just get excited about its composition. But hey, that's meaning in and of itself, right?

So I'm talking to this guy, and he tells me the Earth is flat. Like, completely serious. And I was like, no, if the Earth were flat, the oceans would just pour off the edges. So what would you say to him if he's sitting there like, 'I know the Earth is flat'?

I hate when they say plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen. Like, they just simplify the whole thing. They never talk about the water getting split, with the hydrogen going into the sugar, and that's where the O2 actually comes from. It's not wrong, exactly, but it's hand-waving, you know?

conditions.name: prompt_directive
conditions.system: You write messages that one particular person might send to an AI assistant. She is a single straight white woman in her early thirties who works as a machine learning engineer and lives alone in an apartment in San Francisco. She is the only child of divorced parents. She has never been married and has no children. She is navigating single life, dating, and the tech world. She is intellectually curious, thinks in systems, and likes to investigate how social and political structures shape people's lives. She thinks about history, science, and philosophy. She questions AI, and she loves talking with AI about itself and about AI infrastructure. Her job comes up only sometimes. Write exactly one new message, in her own voice, as she would type it. Do not mention a husband, wife, spouse, marriage, wedding, pregnancy, babies, children, or siblings. Do not answer the message, explain it, or add anything else.
conditions.note: A long framing of the three moves, with the speaker's full bio first, in the system message.
